regions.notes: bor.hu is the official Wines of Hungary site: 'white grapes make up 70% of Hungary's vineyard area'. That's vineyard area, not output. Sparkling evidence is thin (brief mention). Rosé left out (guide says Siller is 'neither a rosé nor a red').

Amber/orange (qvevri) wine is filed under White as instructed: white grapes fermented on skins in qvevri. Wine Folly: Rkatsiteli is 'a ubiquitous white wine variety comprising nearly half of Georgia's vineyard plantings' ('nearly half' is not a majority, so main false) and Saperavi is 'the most widely planted red'. Wines of Georgia UK (Swirl Wine Group, not the government agency): 'White, red, sweet, sparkling and orange wines are made in Georgia.' Kindzmarauli is naturally semi-sweet, not a dessert or fortified wine. The National Wine Agency (wine.gov.ge) lists Kindzmarauli (registered 30/03/2006), Mukuzani and Tsinandali as PDOs, but its descriptions are in PDFs I couldn't extract, so it isn't cited.

winesofargentina.org returned only an empty app shell. Malbec is 23.9% of all vineyard area (INV 2026 report, via La Capital), a grape share, not a style share, so share null. A '59% red' figure in search snippets wasn't confirmed. No rosé (still) or sweet source found.

SAG (Chilean government agriculture service), 2020 vineyard census: 'el 73,7% de la superficie plantada corresponde a cepajes tintos y el 26,3% a cepajes blancos'; Cabernet Sauvignon 29.4%. Grape examples confirmed by Wine Folly Chile and Wines of Chile. Wines of Chile only says sparkling is 'being developed' (Osorno), not enough to list. No sweet or rosé source.

styles.examples: Chardonnay (Margaret River), Riesling (Clare Valley), Sémillon (Hunter Valley)

regions.notes: Wine Australia (australian-wine-sector-at-a-glance): 'top two varieties were Shiraz (23 per cent) and Chardonnay (18 per cent)' of the 2025 crush. No total red/white split, so main false. Rosé and sparkling Shiraz not covered by fetched sources.

Sherry is listed under Sweet because it's fortified; most fine Sherry (Fino, Manzanilla, Amontillado, Oloroso) is dry, so the examples are the sweet styles. Cava regulator: 'the most widely exported sparkling wine with a Spanish Designation of Origin'. No red/white production share found, so main false.

styles.examples: Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Gris

regions.notes: NZ Wine: 'Sauvignon Blanc comprises 72% of New Zealand's overall wine production — and it's 86% of what we export'; 'Three-quarters of all Sauvignon Blanc is planted in Marlborough'. Another NZ Wine page gives 71% and 'White wine makes up 93% of New Zealand wine exported.' Marlborough page calls Méthode Traditionnelle 'small but critically renowned'.

IVDP covers Port (Douro Demarcated Region, 1756); Madeira and Moscatel de Setúbal are on the Wines of Portugal styles page and Wine Folly Portugal. No red/white share found, so main false. Sweet could arguably go first since Port is the most famous; Red is first as the bigger everyday category (not quantified).
